I'm in the market for another hooded nib pen. Currently I have a parker 21 (w/ a ruined nib), and a pilot elite (the cheap one) that I use daily.

What I'd really like is a sheaffer imperial or newer pilot elite, but both of those have prices a bit too steep for me in the gold nibbed versions.

So, what hooded nib pen recommendations do you all have? I'd prefer pens on the cheaper side, but feel free to list whatever you think are the coolest/best of the lot.

EDIT: I said sheaffer imperial so I guess inlaid nibs and the like are fair game too. Actually, anything other than the standard nib style is okay.

Parker 45 is one of them. If it's gold, it has a bit of flex to it.

Obvious one is Lamy 2000, but there's a bit of an adjustment period for it. You have to let it settle in before you notice that it writes fantastic. This can take a week or two.

I wish they had more hooded nibs. I don't like the old antiquated nib design.
Parker 51 is the classic hooded nib pen. I would go for that, or a 61.

I like the Waterm Taperite/stateleigh/crusader because it has a cool design as well as usually a semiflex nib. Parkers are a given, but I particularly like the 61 with the capillary fillers and the falcon/50.
